title: Top 3 true crime cases tied to stories of demons
lines: Top three true crime cases tied to stories of demons.
Number three: Son of Sam.
After shooting six people to death in New York,
David Berkowitz claimed the one giving him orders was his neighbor's black dog.
He said a 6,000-year-old demon had possessed the dog
and used its voice to order him to kill.
Two years later, in a prison interview,
Berkowitz admitted he had made up the demon to excuse his crimes.
It was not until 1987 that he turned to God to beg for forgiveness.
Number two: the Amityville house.
One evening in November 1974,
Ronald DeFeo Jr. ran into a bar, saying his parents had been shot.
Only when friends followed him home did they discover
that all four of his younger siblings were also dead in their bedrooms.
The next day, Ronald confessed that he was the one who had fired the gun.
In court, he said voices had urged him to kill his whole family.
A year later, the Lutz family moved into that house.
Mr. Lutz said that when a priest came to bless it,
the priest heard a voice shout: "Get out!"
The Lutz family lasted only 28 days there.
Number one: the case behind the movie Emily Rose.
Two years after Anneliese Michel died,
her sister heard her voice again, in the middle of a courtroom.
The court was playing a tape recorded during an exorcism.
On the tape, two priests recite prayers,
while Anneliese screams back in a voice almost impossible to recognize.
During those rituals, she sometimes called herself Lucifer, and sometimes Judas.
Anneliese died at the age of 23 from malnutrition and dehydration.
By then, she weighed only about 68 pounds.
Her parents and the two priests sat at the defendants' table.
All four were later convicted of negligent homicide.
